sources.entry: Mole Widget - Lightweight macOS desktop system monitor with live CPU, memory, disk, network, battery, and process metrics, managed from the menu bar.

summary.one_liner: Mole Widget is a lightweight native macOS desktop widget that shows live CPU, memory, disk, network, battery, and process metrics in the terminal style of the mole `mo status` CLI.
keywords: see cpu and ram on my desktop
summary.what_it_does: Mole Widget is a borderless macOS window that sits at desktop level, above the wallpaper and below application windows. It displays sections for header info (chip, RAM, macOS version, uptime, and a 0–100 health score), CPU (total and top-3 cores, load average, SoC temperature, trend sparkline), memory, disk (usage plus read/write speed), power (charge, battery health, cycle count, temperature), network (download/upload sparklines, interface, local IP), and the top three processes by CPU. The menu bar offers optional live CPU, memory, and CPU temperature readouts, plus a Usage History view that keeps up to 12 hours of CPU and RAM data with a scrubber to inspect heavy processes at a past moment. Users can drag the widget, resize its width, lock its position and size, hide it, and configure opacity, visible sections, refresh rate, and font. Updates are handled through Sparkle for both DMG and Homebrew installs.
use_cases: Keep CPU, RAM, and network stats visible on the desktop
Check battery health and cycle count on a MacBook
Find which process is using the most CPU right now
Review CPU and memory history from the past few hours
Show live CPU or memory numbers in the menu bar
Monitor a Mac's performance without opening Activity Monitor
notable: Desktop-level borderless window, visible on all Spaces and ignored by Mission Control and ⌘Tab
Usage History with 1h/4h/12h range and a scrubber to see top processes at any past moment
Menu bar readouts for CPU, memory, and CPU temperature that turn yellow past 60% and red past 85%
Pure-function computation over raw snapshots, with unit-tested math and thin collectors over mach/IOKit
Signed and notarized DMG, Homebrew cask, and Sparkle auto-updates
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and a Swift 6 toolchain to build from source
Tests must be run with make test because a bare swift test silently runs zero tests on machines without full Xcode
Homebrew install relies on Sparkle for updates; the cask declares auto_updates true
